title: Misinformation emerges as Sweden’s election run-up goes into final stage
content:
NORDIS and its Swedish partners Källkritikbyrån and Fojo Media Institute examine how misinformation, AI and election fraud rumours are shaping the Swedish election campaign.

The Swedish election campaign for municipal, regional and national elections is in full swing, marking the beginning of a high season for potential misinformation in Sweden.

NORDIS has spoken to its partners at fact-checking organisation Källkritikbyrån and the Fojo Media Institute at Linnaeus University about the role misinformation has played in the Swedish election campaign so far.

Sweden is an easy target in the information space, because of its reputation as a liberal country. This means both positively, as a perceived successful progressive society and negatively, where it’s claimed to be wrecked by immigrants or too “woke”.

sourceDescription: The Nordic Observatory for Digital Media and Information Disorder

title: New project to support newsrooms against disinformation ahead of Swedish election
content:
Alerts about AI-generated content, independent fact-checking and dedicated support for smaller newsrooms. The project Valkollen 2026 (“The Election Check”) aims to equip Swedish journalists ahead of the upcoming general election. The initiative is led by NORDIS partner Fojo Media Institute at Linnaeus University and made possible by a donation of four million Swedish kronor.

“Ahead of the 2026 election, journalists will face an information landscape where the pace is relentless, the flows overwhelming and attempts at manipulative influence more sophisticated than ever. Valkollen 2026 gives Swedish journalists the tools to counter attempts to manipulate public opinion,” says Andreas Önnerfors, researcher at NORDIS partner Fojo Media Institute and project manager for Valkollen 2026, a project under the umbrella of the Fojo Verify section of the Institute.

title: Hoaxes and misleading claims in the Swedish election campaign
content:
AI-generated clickbait, fake election posters and classic half-truths from politicians – here is NORDIS partner Källkritikbyrån’s major review of the election campaign’s hoaxes and distortions.

Fact-checkers such as Källkritikbyrån and the Valkollen project are monitoring the Swedish election and looking for false and misleading claims. The election campaign is now entering its final stage – here NORDIS partner Källkritikbyrån review what has emerged so far.

Clickbait networks make money from ad clicks during election periods

Excerpt from a Facebook post on 18 May.

Källkritikbyrån has previously exposed a network of Facebook pages that share false and inflammatory content to drive traffic to “news sites” filled with advertisements. The actors behind them include people in Vietnam, who use the method to make money. Last year, the content consisted of AI-generated sob stories, but in January we discovered that the pages were also involving themselves in the case of a missing 18-year-old in Uddevalla and spreading false claims.
